questions.question: How many classes of hazardous materials are there?
questions.explanation: There are nine classes of hazardous materials. Each class shows the type of danger the material poses.

questions.question: What sign might show that a shipment contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
The cargo comes from a supermarket.
The cargo sits on wood pallets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often hold hazardous materials. Take proper safety steps when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: Where should the ID number for a hazardous material appear?
questions.explanation: The ID number must appear on the shipping paper and on the package. It must also appear on cargo tanks and other large containers.

questions.question: What does Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table show?
questions.explanation: Column 2 lists the proper shipping names and descriptions of hazardous materials.

questions.question: Where must a hazardous materials placard be placed?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the outside of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle on the outside.

questions.question: Can the ID number, shipping name, and hazard class be shortened on shipping papers?

options.text: Yes, if using a small piece of paper.
Yes, if the shorthand is easy to understand.

questions.explanation: The ID number, shipping name, and hazard class must not be shortened on shipping papers. Abbreviations are only allowed if the regulations specifically allow them.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of placards needed on a vehicle carrying hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: At least four identical placards must be displayed on the front, back, and both sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous materials label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Put the label on a tag securely attached to the package.
Make the label smaller to fit.
Paste the label on the trailer wall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the label on a tag securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: If a label will not fit on a package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: Which material may need a transport index?
questions.explanation: Some radioactive materials must have a transport index. This number shows how much control the material needs during transport. The total transport index for all cargo in one vehicle cannot exceed 50.

questions.question: Which action should you NOT do when loading hazardous materials?

options.text: Keep hazardous materials away from heat.

questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake before loading or unloading. Do not use hooks or tools that could damage containers. Keep hazardous materials away from heat.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees receive training and testing?
questions.explanation: All drivers must learn about security risks when transporting hazardous materials. Training must cover how to spot and handle security threats. Hazardous materials employees must be trained and tested at least once every three years.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?

options.text: Talk to other hazardous materials drivers.

questions.explanation: The manual has all the information you need to pass the hazardous materials test. But reading it is just the first step. You should also learn federal and state rules about transporting hazardous materials and attend training courses.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in a trailer, how should the trailer be cleaned?

options.text: Let it air dry without washing.

questions.explanation: Any part of a vehicle that touches corrosive liquids must be washed thoroughly with water.

questions.question: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, what are they certifying?

options.text: The package does not contain hazardous materials.
The package was prepared following all rules.
The package was packed at a specific location.
The package will be loaded on the trailer first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The package was prepared following all rules.
questions.explanation: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they certify that the package was prepared following all applicable rules.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation "RQ" mean?
questions.explanation: On shipping papers, "RQ" can be used instead of an "X" in the "HM" column to show that a reportable quantity of hazardous material is present.

questions.question: Which sign suggests a shipment contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipper sells fireworks or munitions.
Your last shipment was labeled hazardous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper sells fireworks or munitions.
questions.explanation: A clue that a shipment may contain hazardous materials is the shipper's type of business. Examples include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, scientific supply stores, pest control companies, farm supply stores, and explosives or fireworks dealers.

questions.question: Hazardous materials regulations protect all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Because hazardous materials are risky, federal, state, and local governments have rules for transporting them. These rules protect the driver, people nearby, and the environment.

questions.question: What license do you need to transport hazardous materials?

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a tank endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: To drive any vehicle carrying hazardous materials, you must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: A vehicle that is not properly placarded:

options.text: Can only be moved in an emergency.
Can be driven if it does not carry radioactive materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle carrying hazardous materials must have proper placards to be driven. An improperly placarded vehicle may only be driven if needed to protect life or property during an emergency.

questions.question: A vehicle that is not properly placarded:

options.text: May only be moved in an emergency.
May be driven if the cargo is not radioactive.

questions.correctAnswerText: May only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle without proper placards for its hazardous materials cargo cannot be driven. The only exception is when necessary to protect life and property in an emergency.

questions.question: Many poisonous products are also:
questions.explanation: Many poisonous materials are also flammable.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials:

options.text: The engine should be left on.
The engine should be turned off.
The gas nozzle may be left unattended.
Someone other than the driver should do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine should be turned off.
questions.explanation: Turn the engine off before refueling. Someone must always watch the nozzle.

questions.question: Your engine runs a pump used to deliver compressed gas. After delivery, turn off the engine ____ unhooking the hoses.
questions.explanation: Turn the engine off after the delivery is complete but before unhooking the hoses.

questions.question: ____ identical placards must be placed on a vehicle carrying hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves open during loading and unloading. Keep them closed at all other times.

questions.question: When you are seated behind the steering wheel, shipping papers should be:

options.text: Taped to the passenger's side window.

questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's door or another spot where you can easily reach them while wearing your seat belt. They must be easy to see.

questions.question: What does a shipping paper describe?

options.text: How the materials will be transported
Who should accept the materials being transported

questions.explanation: Shipping papers describe the specific hazardous materials being transported.

questions.question: If you notice a cargo leak, identify the leaking materials by:
questions.explanation: Use the shipping papers, label, or package location to identify leaking materials. Do not touch or smell them. This could cause injury or death.

questions.question: If a hazardous material package is smaller than its label, how should it be labeled?

options.text: The item may be tied together with other hazardous materials and labeled with a sheet of paper on the outside of the bundle.
The label may be attached to a tag that is securely attached to the package.
The item may be marked with a large orange dot.
The item may be placed in a box displaying a warning label.

questions.correctAnswerText: The label may be attached to a tag that is securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: If a diamond-shaped hazard label doesn't fit on the package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: How long must shippers keep a copy of shipping papers for hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep a copy of shipping papers for at least two years from the date the carrier accepts the material. For hazardous waste, keep them for three years.
